displayText.simplePara: AMPEL360 eWTW, baseline configuration, MSN-001 to MSN-050.

levelledPara.title: Purpose and product role
levelledPara.para: The radome is the forward-most fairing of the aircraft, enclosing the weather-radar antenna. It performs three roles simultaneously: it provides the aerodynamic nose surface; it serves as a radio-frequency window through which the weather radar transmits and receives; and it forms the forward bird-strike and lightning-attachment surface of the airframe.

The radome is located forward of the forward pressure bulkhead and is therefore unpressurized. Cabin pressurization is not a load case for the radome; its structural loads are aerodynamic, bird-strike, and handling.

levelledPara.title: Construction and constituents
levelledPara.para: The radome wall is a radio-frequency-transparent sandwich laminate. Its owned constituents are:

listItem.para: dielectric sandwich core of controlled permittivity;
rain-erosion boot or coating on the leading surface;
attachment, hinge, and latch fittings to the radome backup bulkhead;
bonding and ground provisions for the lightning-protection interface.

levelledPara.title: Dimensional data
levelledPara.para: The radome external form is a secant ogive of fineness ratio approximately 1.36. Absolute dimensional data is provisional pending resolution of the concept-stage CAD scale.

warning.warningAndCautionPara: Dimensional values are not yet authoritative. The conceptual CAD artefact (RADOME-REV-A1) carries an unresolved scale finding; absolute dimensions are TBD until the finding is closed and the revision is released.

levelledPara.title: Functional description
levelledPara.para: As a radio-frequency window, the radome wall is tuned so the weather radar transmits and receives through it with minimal transmission loss and boresight error. The radio-frequency performance requirement is set by the weather-radar system and is met, not defined, by the radome.

As the forward-most surface, the radome sustains bird strike without debris penetrating to the radar or the backup bulkhead. As a lightning-attachment surface in attachment zone 1A, the non-conductive radome relies on diverter strips, mounted by the lightning-protection system, to control attachment.

levelledPara.title: Interfaces
levelledPara.para: The radome attaches structurally to the radome backup bulkhead, which permits removal for radar access.

The radome encloses the weather-radar antenna. The weather-radar system is described separately:
Weather radar Description
.

The lightning diverter strips and bonding network are owned by the lightning-protection system and are described separately:
Lightning protection Description
.

levelledPara.title: Design constraints
levelledPara.para: The radome design is governed by competing constraints: radio-frequency transmission efficiency and boresight error (set by the weather-radar system); bird-strike resistance; lightning attachment in zone 1A; rain erosion of the leading surface; and moisture ingress, which degrades radio-frequency performance and is therefore a radio-frequency constraint as well as a structural one.

caution.warningAndCautionPara: Radio-frequency and bird-strike requirements can conflict: a thinner wall improves transmission but reduces impact resistance. Any change to wall construction, core, coating, or diverter provisions requires joint re-verification of both the radio-frequency performance and the bird-strike and lightning cases.
